claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing revenue.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion.
AWS's AI and custom-silicon businesses each passed a $25 billion annualized run rate.
The 2026 predictions in last year's edition of this piece held up (the prior edition predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade).
According to Gartner, by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner has forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
Gartner describes cloud as becoming a business necessity by 2028.
McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report says cloud value driven by innovation is worth 5x more than cost savings.
McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report says high-performing organizations can achieve EBITDA uplift of 20–30% by 2030.
McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report says Asia leads in projected cloud value, followed by the US and Europe.
AWS reported $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, its fastest revenue growth since 2021, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter.
AWS's AI business and its chips business (including custom Trainium and Graviton silicon) each exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.

Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time, announced in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), with Azure revenue growing 43% year-over-year, up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said: 'This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time.'
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026, and its backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had itself already been raised twice this year.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year.
Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals now totaling $75 billion.
Hyperscalers are making the largest infrastructure investments in cloud history, nearly all centered on AI workloads, inference, and high-performance compute.
ResearchAndMarkets says hybrid cloud will grow from $130B to $310–330B by 2030.
Mordor Intelligence says 87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds.
Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure, with most running more than one.
Hybrid and multi-cloud strategies are now mainstream.
Gartner forecasts total worldwide AI spending, spanning software, hardware, and services, will reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027, half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.
Pulumi has a Superintelligence Infrastructure product perspective page at the linked URL.
Infrastructure as code integrates with third-party services including CockroachDB, Confluent Cloud, and Kafka.
Pulumi Insights Discovery improves cloud resource efficiency and visibility.
Pulumi Policies helps teams detect misconfigurations, analyze usage patterns, and generate infrastructure updates using AI-driven optimization.
Gartner predicts that by 2028, over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms to secure third-party AI service usage and protect custom-built AI applications.
Gartner predicts total spending on securing AI will reach roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
There are 3 key predictions for the future of DevSecOps listed below.
Pulumi ESC helps teams centralize and govern credentials, keys, and tokens.

Carlie Idoine, VP Analyst at Gartner, said at the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in Sydney: 'AI... doesn't deliver value on its own – AI needs to be tightly aligned with data, analytics, and governance to enable intelligent, adaptive decisions and actions across the organization.'

According to Gartner, by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams as internal providers of reusable services, components, and tools for application delivery.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations already have a dedicated platform engineering team, and 35% are running a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.

Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said: 'Cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are not just experimenting but standardizing on CNCF projects that make software delivery reliable at scale... how organizations are extending those same platforms to support AI workloads, showing how cloud native is the base layer of powering the next era of applications.'
Large tech companies are the first adopters of platform engineering practices, and mid-size to large companies continue to invest in them.
Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029.
Gartner predicts human-in-the-loop requirements in IT operations workflows fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 82% agree AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.

In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 63% say they trust agents to make production changes, while manual approval remains close to universal today; Pulumi's report describes this as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, teams expecting agents to generate half or more of their infrastructure code rise from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails in place.
Pulumi's blog post 'The Agentic Infrastructure Era' argues AIOps is headed toward a supervised agentic operating model rather than faster dashboards and alerting alone.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.
CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%.
CNCF's Q3 2025 report says 30% of backend developers now use Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, a decline the report attributes to the technology's growing maturity.

Inference workloads powered by LLMs and GPUs now require low-latency execution closer to the user, often leveraging Kubernetes as the common control plane for AI cluster orchestration across edge and core clusters.
Kubernetes supports AI through GPU-aware scheduling and more advanced workload orchestration.

According to Gartner, by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use dedicated AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use AI code assistants.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit (announced May 2026).
Mirantis's Lens has launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor have moved from novelty to everyday tooling for a large share of enterprise software teams.

Pulumi Agent Skills is a collection of infrastructure expertise packaged for AI coding assistants that teaches tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to reason about Pulumi projects, reducing hallucination.
Pulumi has a Remote MCP Server that provides infrastructure access to AI assistants, with Pulumi Neo executing actions with previews, policies, and orchestration.
AI code assistants are fast becoming a competitive advantage in cloud software development.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
Modern IaC, unified governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks are all core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.
The post's title, title_tag, meta_desc and intro frame these as trends shaping 2027.
The post was last updated 2026-09-15.
